# Pet Care Guide — Overview

> Sample documentation about caring for pets. All content is fictional placeholder text for a PoC.

This guide covers the basics of choosing, feeding, and caring for common household pets.

## Pets

- **[Dogs](./dogs.md)** — loyal, active companions that need daily exercise.
- **[Cats](./cats.md)** — independent pets that still need play and attention.
- **[Small pets](./small-pets.md)** — rabbits, guinea pigs, and hamsters.
- **[Fish](./fish.md)** — calm pets that depend on water quality.

## Care topics

- **[Nutrition](./nutrition.md)** — what and how much to feed.
- **[Vaccinations](./vaccinations.md)** — the core schedule for dogs and cats.
- **[Grooming](./grooming.md)** — brushing, bathing, and nail care.
- **[Training](./training.md)** — positive reinforcement basics.
- **[Health signs](./health-signs.md)** — when to call the vet.

New pet owner? Start with [Choosing a pet](./choosing-a-pet.md).

source: docs/choosing-a-pet.md

# Choosing a pet

Match the pet to your home, schedule, and budget.

| Pet                         | Daily time   | Space needed | Typical lifespan |
|-----------------------------|--------------|--------------|------------------|
| [Dog](./dogs.md)            | 1–3 hours    | Medium–large | 10–15 years      |
| [Cat](./cats.md)            | 30–60 min    | Small–medium | 12–18 years      |
| [Rabbit](./small-pets.md)   | 1–2 hours    | Medium       | 8–12 years       |
| [Hamster](./small-pets.md)  | 15–30 min    | Small        | 2–3 years        |
| [Fish](./fish.md)           | 10–15 min    | Small        | Varies           |

## Questions to ask yourself

1. Who will handle [feeding](./nutrition.md) and [grooming](./grooming.md) every day?
2. Can you afford [vaccinations](./vaccinations.md) and vet visits?
3. Do you have time for [training](./training.md)?

Back to [Overview](./overview.md)

# Dogs

Dogs are social animals that need daily exercise, structure, and companionship.

## Exercise needs by size

| Size   | Example breeds              | Daily exercise |
|--------|-----------------------------|----------------|
| Small  | Chihuahua, Pug              | 30–60 min      |
| Medium | Beagle, Border Collie       | 1–2 hours      |
| Large  | Labrador, German Shepherd   | 1–2 hours      |

## Essentials

- Feed a complete diet — see [Nutrition](./nutrition.md).
- Keep [vaccinations](./vaccinations.md) up to date, including rabies.
- Start [training](./training.md) early with positive reinforcement.
- Brush regularly — see [Grooming](./grooming.md).

Watch for the warning signs in [Health signs](./health-signs.md).

Compare with [Cats](./cats.md) · Back to [Overview](./overview.md)

---
source: docs/cats.md
---

# Cats

Cats are independent but still need daily play, a clean litter box, and regular vet care.

## Essentials

- **Litter box:** one per cat plus one extra, scooped daily.
- **Play:** two 10–15 minute sessions a day to prevent boredom.
- **Scratching:** provide a sturdy scratching post.
- **Diet:** cats are obligate carnivores — see [Nutrition](./nutrition.md).
- **Vaccines:** see the cat schedule in [Vaccinations](./vaccinations.md).

## Indoor vs outdoor

Indoor cats generally live longer and avoid traffic, fights, and parasites.

Long-haired breeds need more [grooming](./grooming.md). Changes in litter habits are a key item in [Health signs](./health-signs.md).

Compare with [Dogs](./dogs.md) · Back to [Overview](./overview.md)

---
source: docs/small-pets.md

# Small pets

Rabbits, guinea pigs, and hamsters are good options for smaller homes, but each has specific needs.

| Pet        | Diet basics                         | Social?               |
|------------|-------------------------------------|-----------------------|
| Rabbit     | Unlimited hay, leafy greens, pellets | Yes — keep in pairs   |
| Guinea pig | Hay, vitamin C–rich vegetables       | Yes — keep in pairs   |
| Hamster    | Seed mix, small amounts of veggies   | No — keep alone       |

## Tips

- Rabbits and guinea pigs need hay at all times for teeth and digestion — see [Nutrition](./nutrition.md).
- Nails need trimming every 4–6 weeks — see [Grooming](./grooming.md).
- Rabbits can be litter-trained — see [Training](./training.md).
- Small pets hide illness; check [Health signs](./health-signs.md) often.

Back to [Choosing a pet](./choosing-a-pet.md) · [Overview](./overview.md)

source: docs/fish.md

# Fish

Fish are low-maintenance day to day, but their health depends on stable water.

## Tank setup

1. Choose the largest tank you can — bigger tanks stay stable more easily.
2. Add a filter and heater (for tropical fish).
3. **Cycle the tank** for 4–6 weeks before adding fish.
4. Add a few fish at a time.

## Water care

| Task                | How often   |
|---------------------|-------------|
| Test water          | Weekly      |
| Partial water change (20–25%) | Weekly |
| Rinse filter media in tank water | Monthly |

Feed only what they eat in two minutes — see [Nutrition](./nutrition.md). Cloudy eyes, clamped fins, or gasping at the surface are listed in [Health signs](./health-signs.md).

Back to [Choosing a pet](./choosing-a-pet.md) · [Overview](./overview.md)

source: docs/nutrition.md

# Nutrition

Good nutrition is the foundation of pet health.

## General rules

- Feed a complete, balanced diet made for the species and life stage.
- Measure portions; obesity is the most common nutrition problem.
- Fresh water must always be available.
- Change foods gradually over 7–10 days.

## By pet

| Pet                         | Key point                                          |
|-----------------------------|----------------------------------------------------|
| [Dogs](./dogs.md)           | Two meals a day for adults; adjust for activity    |
| [Cats](./cats.md)           | Need animal protein and taurine; wet food helps hydration |
| [Small pets](./small-pets.md) | Hay should be most of the diet for rabbits and guinea pigs |
| [Fish](./fish.md)           | Small amounts once or twice a day                  |

## Toxic foods

Never feed chocolate, grapes, raisins, onions, garlic, xylitol, or alcohol. If your pet eats one, see [Health signs](./health-signs.md) and call your vet.

Back to [Overview](./overview.md)

# Vaccinations

Vaccines protect pets from serious diseases. Your vet will tailor the schedule; this is a general example.

## Dogs

| Age          | Vaccines                                   |
|--------------|--------------------------------------------|
| 6–8 weeks    | Distemper, parvovirus                      |
| 10–12 weeks  | DHPP (distemper, hepatitis, parainfluenza, parvo) |
| 12–16 weeks  | Rabies, DHPP booster                       |
| Yearly / every 3 years | Boosters as advised              |

## Cats

| Age          | Vaccines                                   |
|--------------|--------------------------------------------|
| 6–8 weeks    | FVRCP                                      |
| 10–12 weeks  | FVRCP booster, FeLV (if at risk)           |
| 12–16 weeks  | Rabies, FVRCP booster                      |

Mild tiredness after a vaccine is normal; swelling of the face or trouble breathing is an emergency — see [Health signs](./health-signs.md).

See also: [Dogs](./dogs.md) · [Cats](./cats.md) · [Overview](./overview.md)

---
source: docs/grooming.md

# Grooming

Regular grooming keeps coats healthy and lets you spot problems early.

| Task          | Dogs                  | Cats                   | Small pets          |
|---------------|-----------------------|------------------------|---------------------|
| Brushing      | 1–7× per week by coat | 1–2× per week (daily for long hair) | Weekly; daily when shedding |
| Bathing       | Every 1–3 months      | Rarely                 | Avoid (spot clean)  |
| Nail trimming | Every 3–4 weeks       | Every 2–3 weeks        | Every 4–6 weeks     |
| Teeth         | Brush several times a week | Brush if tolerated | Hay wears teeth down |

## Tips

- Make grooming positive with treats — see [Training](./training.md).
- While brushing, check for lumps, ticks, and sore spots — see [Health signs](./health-signs.md).

Pet guides: [Dogs](./dogs.md) · [Cats](./cats.md) · [Small pets](./small-pets.md)

---
source: docs/training.md

# Training

Positive reinforcement — rewarding the behavior you want — is the most effective and humane training method.

## Basics

1. **Reward right away** (within 1–2 seconds) with a treat or praise.
2. **Keep sessions short:** 5–10 minutes, a few times a day.
3. **Be consistent:** everyone in the house uses the same words.
4. **Never punish** — it creates fear and makes training harder.

## First commands for dogs

`sit`, `down`, `stay`, `come`, and `leave it`. See [Dogs](./dogs.md).

## Other pets

- [Cats](./cats.md) can learn to use a scratching post and come when called.
- Rabbits can be litter-trained — see [Small pets](./small-pets.md).

Use small, healthy treats and count them in the daily [nutrition](./nutrition.md) budget.

Back to [Overview](./overview.md)

# Health signs

Know what's normal for your pet so you notice changes early.

## Call the vet today if you see

- Not eating for more than 24 hours (12 hours for [small pets](./small-pets.md)).
- Vomiting or diarrhea lasting more than a day.
- Changes in litter box use or straining to pee — urgent for male [cats](./cats.md).
- Limping, lumps, or sudden weight change.

## Emergency — go now

- Trouble breathing or a swollen face (possible [vaccine](./vaccinations.md) reaction).
- Eating something toxic — see the list in [Nutrition](./nutrition.md).
- Collapse, seizures, or a swollen, hard belly in [dogs](./dogs.md).
- [Fish](./fish.md) gasping at the surface (test the water right away).

Regular [grooming](./grooming.md) is a good time to check for problems.

Back to [Overview](./overview.md)
